answer: The distribution of RNA expression data is HIGHLY RIGHT-SKEWED. Fisher–Pearson (moment) skewness of the pooled raw expression values (all 20,502 genes × 328 TCGA-COAD samples, n = 6,724,656) is g1 ≈ 42.44 (far above the |g1| ≥ 1.0 "highly skewed" threshold). Supporting evidence: mean (932.0) is ~5.3× the median (176.8), 15.24% of values are exactly zero, and the bulk histogram shows a sharp peak near 0 with a long right tail extending to ~1.34×10⁶ (p99 ≈ 10,879 vs p50 ≈ 177). Sensitivity checks: on a log1p scale the data is nearly symmetric (g1 ≈ −0.30), and the per-sample mean-expression profile is also right-skewed (g1 ≈ 1.31) — but as supplied (untransformed, FPKM/TPM-like values), the distribution is highly right-skewed.
